cohort: The study included 416 Colombian children under five years old.
finding: Various early-life environmental exposures (e.g., PM2.5, NO2, in-house cockroaches, crowding, humidity, walkability), dietary factors (soft drinks, cereals), and genetic polymorphisms (GSTM1, H2AX, OGG1) were significantly associated with either increased or decreased DNA damage in children, with notable gene-environment interactions.
